title: Helmsman: conservative SLO-aware routing & safe-config conductor for batching/caching optimizations
creator: Maya Patel
description: Implement a conservative orchestration layer (Helmsman) that safely applies batching and caching recommendations by combining per-route SLO fences, cohort-based traffic shaping, SLO-aware routing decisions, and causal anomaly detection. The goal is to realize sustained cost savings from automated config changes while keeping latency and throughput SLOs intact and ensuring rapid automated rollback when regressions are detected.
background: We have a pipeline for generating batching/caching recommendations, but previous rollouts caused intermittent p95 regressions in several routes when applied broadly. Existing staged rollouts and canary windows are effective but lack a unified conductor that 1) reasons about cross-route SLO correlations, 2) enforces a conservative ramp policy by default, and 3) ties anomaly detection to automated rollback and routing fallbacks. Helmsman addresses these gaps.
proposal:
Build a Helmsman service that: 
- consumes recommended config diffs (batch size, prefetch thresholds, KV cache policies) from the optimizer engine,
- assigns risk scores using a lightweight causal drift detector (CDDT) that compares live metric deltas against historical micro-window baselines,
- computes safe apply percentages per-cohort using an epsilon-greedy conservative ramp (start 1%-5% traffic, exponential backoff to a max safe cap),
- enforces per-route SLO fences (latency p95, error rate, throughput) and a global budgeted circuit-limiter to avoid noisy neighbor effects,
- implements SLO-aware routing where traffic is dynamically steered to fallback model variants or regions when cohort performance crosses thresholds,
- integrates with the rollout controller to perform automated rollback and creates a prioritized remediation ticket with artifact links on detected regressions.
design_decisions: Use micro-windowing (30s windows aggregated to 5-min baselines) rather than single-point comparisons to reduce sensitivity to transient spikes.
Score config changes by synthetic impact estimate + observed delta; require both low synthetic risk and no real-world signal before expanding traffic allocation.
Default ramp is extremely conservative (1% -> 5% -> 15%) with operator-configurable accelerators for low-risk routes.
Anomaly detector will be causal-first: test for distributional shift on latency and throughput conditioned on request cohort (model, seq_len, tenant tier) rather than global aggregates.
Primary rollback action is immediate traffic reversion + model-variant fallback; secondary action is pausing other in-flight Helmsman applies.
Store immutable audit entries for every apply/rollback for compliance and postmortem analysis.
Expose a dry-run mode and an observed shadow mode for 24h evaluation before any live apply on higher-risk customers.
Integrate with Console alerts and Slack escalation paths for human-in-the-loop confirmation when automation detects high-severity regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Helmsman ingests optimizer diffs and creates an actionable rollout plan for >=3 test routes.
Default conservative ramp executes automatically and expands traffic only when no SLO breaches are detected for the configured observation window (>=15m).
Causal drift detector (CDDT) produces risk scores correlated with actual post-apply regressions in a validation run (AUC >= 0.78 on historical sim).
Automated rollback completes within 60s of breach detection and returns traffic to pre-apply routing without errors >0.5%.
SLO-aware routing matrix can route to at least one fallback model variant/region and the switch completes with <200ms additional latency overhead.
Audit log contains immutable entries for each apply/rollback including config diff, cohorts affected, risk score, and links to artifacts.
Runbook/Playbook documented and linked in Confluence; on-call runbook validated by SRE during staging demo.

testing_plan: 1) Unit tests for CDDT and ramp controller. 2) Integration tests in staging with shadow traffic capture. 3) Backtest Helmsman on last 90 days of recommendation history; measure false positive/negative rollback rates. 4) Synthetic spike tests to ensure rollback executes within SLO. 5) Observability validation: Grafana dashboards for risk score, apply windows, rollback counts, and per-route p95 deltas.
monitoring_and_alerting: Create Grafana panels: Helmsman risk heatmap, apply velocity, rollback latency, per-cohort p95 delta. Configure Alertmanager rules: P0 (automated rollback triggered), P1 (risk score > 0.8 sustained 5m), P2 (dry-run anomalies). Alerts post to #helmsman-ops and on-call SRE paged for P0.

open_questions: What should be the default escalation cadence for false positive rollbacks? (auto reapply after X hours with adjusted conservative thresholds?)
Should we expose a per-tenant risk tolerance knob in Console (enterprise customers may accept higher risk for cost)?
How to treat mixed-cohort requests (requests that hit multiple route classifiers) for cohort-conditioned checks?
What's the allowed maximum of concurrent Helmsman applies globally to prevent global churn?
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Overaggressive automation triggers rollbacks too often and causes thrash. Mitigation: Use hysteresis windows and require both risk score and observed metric breach before rollback.
Risk: CDDT false negatives miss regressions. Mitigation: Shadow runs + staged increase and mandatory final passive observation window before performing >20% traffic applies.
Risk: No fallback model variant available for some routes. Mitigation: Default to regional reroute or pause apply and alert to SRE/Product to create manual fallback plan.
Risk: Audit/compliance requirements for enterprise customers. Mitigation: Add opt-out policy and longer dry-run windows for opted-in customers; keep immutable audit trail.
